items.title: The queue that moved

choices.B: Define the request-to-pickup process, shared dispatch resources and priority rules before choosing another intervention.
choices.C: Measure portal adoption first and use that as the project success measure.
choices.D: Optimize portal response time because it is the controlled subsystem.

items.scenario: The design team finds that a proposed shared power supply meets nominal load but lacks evidence for the worst-case startup combination. The sponsor asks what must be decided before purchasing hardware.
items.question: Which opening best answers that audience?

choices.A: Power supplies are electronic devices that transform one voltage into another.
choices.B: The architecture has a resource-allocation nonconformance requiring systemic disposition.
choices.C: The shared supply is unsafe and should be replaced immediately.
choices.D: The nominal-load check passed. Purchasing depends on confirming startup capacity or choosing a supply with adequate demonstrated margin; the startup combination has not yet been tested.

items.title: The WWW proposal in its context
items.scenario: Tim Berners-Lee's 1989 proposal for CERN emphasizes heterogeneous systems, decentralized links and access to existing information. Security and accounting are secondary concerns in that local proposal.
items.question: Which summary preserves the meaning when explaining it to a modern product team?

choices.A: The proposal recommends one central database to standardize all information.
choices.B: The proposal cannot inform modern design because its requirements are old.
choices.C: The proposal addresses CERN's information-sharing constraints; its priorities explain that concept but do not settle a modern product's security requirements.
choices.D: The proposal argues that security should be secondary in networked products.

items.title: Reporting disagreement

items.title: Explaining verification and validation
items.scenario: A junior engineer asks why a product can pass every specified test and still fail its users. The team has measured compliance with its written requirements but has not observed the intended users in the operating context.
items.question: Which explanation is most accurate?

choices.A: User studies replace requirement testing once a prototype exists.
choices.B: The tests must have been executed incorrectly because passing requirements implies user success.
choices.C: Validation is a synonym for independent repetition of the same tests.
choices.D: Verification assesses the specified requirements; validation examines whether the system serves the intended use and stakeholder needs. A correct implementation of an incomplete or mistaken specification can pass those tests.

items.title: San Bruno: a digital record inherits an error
items.scenario: The NTSB's 2011 San Bruno report traces an erroneous seamless-pipe description from an older accounting record into later records and the GIS. Physical investigation found welded pipe sections.
items.question: What is the best lesson for a digital engineering baseline?

choices.A: Require a second database containing the same imported attributes.
choices.B: Use the newest digital record whenever documents disagree.
choices.C: Discard all historical records and rebuild only from memory.
choices.D: Trace critical attributes to their originating evidence and resolve discrepancies against appropriate inspection or records; digitization does not establish truth.

items.title: A catalog title is not a clause
items.scenario: A standards publisher's public catalog confirms a standard's title and edition. A vendor blog claims a particular clause requires a tool qualification level. The adopted licensed text is unavailable.
items.question: Which statement is supported now?

choices.A: The title and edition are confirmed; the precise clause obligation remains unverified and needs the applicable text or another authoritative basis.
choices.B: The vendor's statement becomes normative because it names the confirmed edition.
choices.C: The clause is false because the licensed text cannot be accessed.
choices.D: Any tool can be used until the clause is verified.

items.title: TCP: acknowledgment at the right layer
items.scenario: RFC 793 (1981) explains that TCP acknowledgment means the receiving TCP has taken responsibility for data, not necessarily that it has been delivered to the end user. A system logs TCP acknowledgment as proof that a remote operator acted.
items.question: What should the review conclude?

choices.A: Replacing TCP with a newer transport protocol resolves the semantic gap.
choices.B: TCP acknowledgments are unreliable and should not be recorded.
choices.C: The log supports transport-level receipt but not operator action; the application/workflow needs its own relevant acknowledgment evidence.
choices.D: The operator action is established whenever both endpoints use TCP.

items.title: DNS: a historical design trade
items.scenario: RFC 1034 (1987) describes distributed maintenance and caching, including a trade among acquisition cost, update speed and cache accuracy. A team proposes a very long cache lifetime to reduce server load for rapidly changing control data.
items.question: What transfers from the source?

choices.B: The trade must be evaluated against this application's update and stale-data consequences; the historical mechanism does not supply its acceptance limits.
choices.C: Caching should be avoided whenever data can change.
choices.D: A cache hit demonstrates that the value is current.

items.title: An identifier survives a changed claim

items.title: Boston I-90: the load duration matters

choices.C: Whether another project previously used any adhesive anchor successfully.
choices.D: Whether the peak proof load exceeds the operating load, as the sole acceptance condition.

items.title: Contradictory views in one baseline
items.scenario: A requirements file says local stop latches until explicit resume. A state diagram automatically resumes after data returns. The test plan checks only fault indication. All three artifacts carry the same release label.
